description: REGRESSION WALL: an event-handler BODY is opaque to the static rule, so this program is CLEAN at `check()` (issue #1155). It looks like it should be a fault — there is no `repeat` anywhere — and an earlier draft of the rule reported it. That was a false positive, and the measurement that settles it is one handler in one lexical position with two outcomes: `repeat 1 [ on_key "a" [ print repcount ] ]` followed by `repeat 3 [ wait 1 ]` PRINTS 1, reading the *dispatching* loop's turn, while the same program followed by a bare `wait 1` raises `ol-repcount-outside-repeat` at `runtime`. A handler body's `repcount` resolves against the repeat stack at DISPATCH time, which no static walk can know — so reporting it here would refuse a program that prints correctly whenever the key arrives during a `repeat`, and since #815 put a severity gate in front of `execute()` that refusal blocks the run. This fixture fails the moment the rule starts judging handler bodies lexically again, in EITHER direction (transparent or boundary — both report here). The fault is not lost: it stays a `runtime` finding when the handler actually fires.
